    "prepare": {
      "filename": "prepare.star",
      "content": "# macports/prepare.star - Prepare phase for MacPorts
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# MacPorts absolutely requires Command Line Tools (CLT) before installation.
# Without CLT, the .pkg installer will fail silently or ports will fail to build.
# After Xcode updates, the license MUST be accepted or builds fail with cryptic errors.

def prepare():
    """Check prerequisites for MacPorts installation."""
    if platform.os != "darwin":
        fail("MacPorts only supports macOS")
    
    _check_command_line_tools()
    _accept_xcode_license()
    _check_existing_installation()
    
    return {"prepare": True}

def _check_command_line_tools():
    """Verify Command Line Tools are installed."""
    result = shell.exec(
        "xcode-select -p",
        allowed_commands=["xcode-select"],
    )
    
    if not result.success or "/CommandLineTools" not in result.stdout:
        # Attempt to install CLT
        shell.exec(
            "xcode-select --install",
            allowed_commands=["xcode-select"],
        )
        fail("Command Line Tools installation initiated. Please complete and retry.")

def _accept_xcode_license():
    """Accept Xcode license if not already accepted."""
    # Check if license needs acceptance
    result = shell.exec(
        "xcodebuild -checkFirstLaunchStatus",
        allowed_commands=["xcodebuild"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        # License needs acceptance
        shell.exec(
            "sudo xcodebuild -license accept",
            allowed_commands=["xcodebuild"],
        )

def _check_existing_installation():
    """Check for existing MacPorts installation."""
    if fs.exists("/opt/local/bin/port"):
        # Check if it's working or needs migration
        result = shell.exec(
            "/opt/local/bin/port version",
            allowed_commands=["port"],
        )
        
        if not result.success:
            # Existing installation is broken - likely needs migration
            print("Warning: Existing MacPorts installation appears broken")
            print("This may require migration after OS upgrade")

def rollback():
    """No rollback needed for prepare phase."""
    pass"
    },
    "install": {
      "filename": "install.star",
      "content": "# macports/install.star - Install phase for MacPorts
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# MacPorts .pkg installers are version-specific and must match your exact macOS version.
# Using the wrong .pkg will either fail to install or cause subtle compatibility issues.
# The install method precedence is: pkg (recommended) > source > git (dev only)

import re

# MacPorts version and supported OS versions
MACPORTS_VERSION = "2.11.6"

# Mapping of macOS versions to codenames for .pkg downloads
MACOS_CODENAMES = {
    "15": "Sequoia",
    "14": "Sonoma", 
    "13": "Ventura",
    "12": "Monterey",
    "11": "BigSur",
    "10.15": "Catalina",
    "10.14": "Mojave",
    "10.13": "HighSierra",
    "10.12": "Sierra",
    "10.11": "ElCapitan",
    "10.10": "Yosemite",
}

def install():
    """Install MacPorts using the best available method."""
    if platform.os != "darwin":
        fail("MacPorts only supports macOS")
    
    # Try pkg installer first (recommended)
    if _try_pkg_install():
        return {"install": True}
    
    # Fall back to source installation
    _install_from_source()
    return {"install": True}

def _try_pkg_install():
    """Attempt to install using version-specific .pkg installer."""
    macos_version = platform.version
    major_version = macos_version.split('.')[0]
    
    # Handle macOS 11+ (single digit) vs 10.x versions
    if int(major_version) >= 11:
        version_key = major_version
    else:
        version_key = '.'.join(macos_version.split('.')[:2])
    
    codename = MACOS_CODENAMES.get(version_key)
    if not codename:
        print(f"No .pkg available for macOS {macos_version}, falling back to source")
        return False
    
    # Construct download URL
    pkg_name = f"MacPorts-{MACPORTS_VERSION}-{version_key}-{codename}.pkg"
    pkg_url = f"https://github.com/macports/macports-base/releases/download/v{MACPORTS_VERSION}/{pkg_name}"
    temp_pkg = f"/tmp/{pkg_name}"
    
    try:
        # Download .pkg
        http.download(pkg_url, temp_pkg)
        
        # Install .pkg
        result = shell.exec(
            f"sudo installer -pkg {temp_pkg} -target /",
            allowed_commands=["installer"],
        )
        
        # Cleanup
        fs.remove(temp_pkg)
        
        return result.success
    except:
        print(f"Failed to download or install .pkg for macOS {macos_version}")
        return False

def _install_from_source():
    """Install MacPorts from source tarball."""
    tarball_name = f"MacPorts-{MACPORTS_VERSION}.tar.bz2"
    tarball_url = f"https://github.com/macports/macports-base/releases/download/v{MACPORTS_VERSION}/{tarball_name}"
    temp_dir = f"/tmp/MacPorts-{MACPORTS_VERSION}"
    temp_tarball = f"/tmp/{tarball_name}"
    
    # Download source
    http.download(tarball_url, temp_tarball)
    
    # Extract
    shell.exec(
        f"tar xjf {temp_tarball} -C /tmp",
        allowed_commands=["tar"],
    )
    
    # Configure, make, install
    shell.exec(
        f"cd {temp_dir} && ./configure",
        allowed_commands=["configure"],
    )
    
    shell.exec(
        f"cd {temp_dir} && make",
        allowed_commands=["make"],
    )
    
    shell.exec(
        f"cd {temp_dir} && sudo make install",
        allowed_commands=["make"],
    )
    
    # Cleanup
    fs.remove(temp_dir)
    fs.remove(temp_tarball)

def rollback():
    """Remove MacPorts installation."""
    # Export installed ports first for user reference
    if fs.exists("/opt/local/bin/port"):
        shell.exec(
            "/opt/local/bin/port -qv installed > ~/macports-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).txt",
            allowed_commands=["port"],
        )
        
        # Uninstall all ports
        shell.exec(
            "sudo /opt/local/bin/port -f uninstall installed",
            allowed_commands=["port"],
        )
    
    # Remove macports user (macOS 10.15+ requirement)
    shell.exec(
        "sudo dscl . -delete /Users/macports",
        allowed_commands=["dscl"],
    )
    
    # Remove macports group
    shell.exec(
        "sudo dscl . -delete /Groups/macports",
        allowed_commands=["dscl"],
    )
    
    # Remove all MacPorts files
    shell.exec(
        "sudo rm -rf /opt/local /Applications/MacPorts /Library/LaunchAgents/org.macports.* /Library/LaunchDaemons/org.macports.*",
        allowed_commands=["rm"],
    )"
    },
    "provision": {
      "filename": "provision.star",
      "content": "# macports/provision.star - Provision phase for MacPorts
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# MacPorts requires selfupdate immediately after installation to sync with
# the current ports tree. Without this, port installations will fail because
# the local ports database is empty or outdated.
#
# PATH setup is critical - users frequently can't find 'port' command because
# /opt/local/bin isn't in their PATH.

def provision():
    """Configure MacPorts for use."""
    _setup_path()
    _initial_selfupdate()
    _configure_variants()
    
    return {"provision": True}

def _setup_path():
    """Add MacPorts paths to user environment."""
    macports_paths = [
        "/opt/local/bin",
        "/opt/local/sbin"
    ]
    
    # Add to common shell profiles
    shell_profiles = [
        "~/.bash_profile",
        "~/.bashrc", 
        "~/.zshrc",
        "~/.profile"
    ]
    
    path_export = 'export PATH="/opt/local/bin:/opt/local/sbin:$PATH"'
    
    for profile in shell_profiles:
        expanded_profile = env.expand(profile)
        if fs.exists(expanded_profile):
            # Check if PATH is already configured
            content = fs.read(expanded_profile)
            if "/opt/local/bin" not in content:
                fs.write(expanded_profile, content + "\n" + path_export + "\n", append=True)

def _initial_selfupdate():
    """Perform initial selfupdate to sync ports tree."""
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE: This is the most critical step.
    # Without selfupdate, the ports tree is empty and nothing will install.
    result = shell.exec(
        "sudo /opt/local/bin/port -v selfupdate",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        fail("Initial selfupdate failed. Check network connectivity and try again.")

def _configure_variants():
    """Configure variant settings if enabled."""
    if not env.get("MACPORTS_VARIANTS", "true").lower() == "true":
        return
    
    macports_conf = "/opt/local/etc/macports/macports.conf"
    
    # Read current config
    if fs.exists(macports_conf):
        config = fs.read(macports_conf)
        
        # Add common variant configurations
        additions = [
            "# Common variant preferences",
            "+universal",  # Enable universal variant by default
            "# macosx_deployment_target ${platform.os_major}.${platform.os_minor}"
        ]
        
        # Only add if not already present
        if "# Common variant preferences" not in config:
            fs.write(macports_conf, config + "\n" + "\n".join(additions) + "\n", append=True)

def rollback():
    """Remove MacPorts configuration."""
    # Remove PATH additions from shell profiles
    shell_profiles = [
        "~/.bash_profile",
        "~/.bashrc",
        "~/.zshrc", 
        "~/.profile"
    ]
    
    for profile in shell_profiles:
        expanded_profile = env.expand(profile)
        if fs.exists(expanded_profile):
            content = fs.read(expanded_profile)
            # Remove MacPorts PATH line
            lines = content.split("\n")
            filtered_lines = [line for line in lines if "/opt/local/bin" not in line or "export PATH=" not in line]
            fs.write(expanded_profile, "\n".join(filtered_lines))"
    },
    "verify": {
      "filename": "verify.star",
      "content": "# macports/verify.star - Verify phase for MacPorts
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# A working MacPorts installation should be able to:
# 1. Report its version (basic functionality)
# 2. List installed ports (database access)
# 3. Search for available ports (network connectivity)
# 4. Show port info (ports tree is synced)

def verify():
    """Verify MacPorts installation is working correctly."""
    if not _verify_basic_functionality():
        return {"verify": False}
    
    if not _verify_database_access():
        return {"verify": False}
    
    if not _verify_ports_tree():
        return {"verify": False}
    
    return {"verify": True}

def _verify_basic_functionality():
    """Test basic port command functionality."""
    result = shell.exec(
        "port version",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        print("ERROR: 'port version' command failed")
        return False
    
    if "Version:" not in result.stdout:
        print("ERROR: Unexpected output from 'port version'")
        return False
    
    print(f"✓ MacPorts version check passed: {result.stdout.strip()}")
    return True

def _verify_database_access():
    """Test database access by listing installed ports."""
    result = shell.exec(
        "port installed",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        print("ERROR: 'port installed' command failed")
        return False
    
    # Should at least show headers even if no ports installed
    if "currently installed:" not in result.stdout.lower():
        print("ERROR: Unexpected output from 'port installed'")
        return False
    
    print("✓ MacPorts database access verified")
    return True

def _verify_ports_tree():
    """Test ports tree by searching for a common port."""
    # Search for 'git' - a port that should always exist
    result = shell.exec(
        "port search --name-glob git",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        print("ERROR: 'port search' command failed")
        print("This usually means the ports tree is not synced")
        print("Try running: sudo port selfupdate")
        return False
    
    if "git @" not in result.stdout:
        print("ERROR: Port search returned unexpected results")
        print("Ports tree may not be properly synced")
        return False
    
    print("✓ MacPorts ports tree access verified")
    return True

def _verify_path_setup():
    """Verify MacPorts is in PATH."""
    port_path = shell.exec(
        "which port",
        allowed_commands=["which"],
    )
    
    if not port_path.success or "/opt/local/bin/port" not in port_path.stdout:
        print("WARNING: MacPorts not found in PATH")
        print("Add this to your shell profile:")
        print('export PATH="/opt/local/bin:/opt/local/sbin:$PATH"')
        return False
    
    return True

def rollback():
    """No rollback needed for verification."""

      "filename": "README.md",
      "content": "# macports

The MacPorts Project provides a comprehensive package management system for macOS, allowing easy installation and management of open source software. MacPorts compiles, installs and upgrades Unix software on macOS, with over 25,000 ported software packages available.

## Features

| Feature | Description | Default |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| **variants** | Build ports with variant support for customization | `true` |
| **migration-support** | Support for OS upgrade migration | `true` |

## Settings

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---------|------|---------|-------------|
| **prefix** | string | `/opt/local` | Installation prefix for MacPorts |
| **build_arch** | string | `` | Target architecture for builds (auto-detected, clear after OS upgrade) |
| **universal_archs** | string | `` | Architectures for universal builds (clear after OS upgrade) |

## Installation Methods

MacPorts supports three installation methods:

1. **PKG Installer (Recommended)**: Version-specific .pkg files for each macOS version
2. **Source Build**: Compile from source tarball
3. **Git**: For developers tracking latest changes

## OS Upgrade Migration

**Critical**: MacPorts requires migration after major macOS upgrades. The package will attempt modern migration (MacPorts 2.10.0+) using `sudo port migrate`, which automatically handles rebuilding incompatible ports.

## Verification

The package verifies MacPorts functionality through:
- Basic command execution (`port version`)
- Database access (`port installed`) 
- Ports tree synchronization (`port search`)

## Dependencies

- **Command Line Tools for Xcode**: Required for all compilation
- **Xcode**: Optional, needed for some ports that build from source

## Tribal Knowledge

### Version-Specific PKG Installers
*Reference: install.star:25-65*

MacPorts .pkg installers are tightly coupled to specific macOS versions. Using the wrong .pkg will either fail to install or cause subtle compatibility issues. The package automatically detects your macOS version and downloads the correct installer.

### Command Line Tools Verification
*Reference: prepare.star:18-32*

MacPorts absolutely requires Command Line Tools before installation. The installer will fail silently without CLT, and ports will fail to build with cryptic errors. Always verify CLT installation with `xcode-select -p` before proceeding.

### Xcode License Acceptance
*Reference: prepare.star:34-47*

After Xcode updates, the license MUST be accepted or builds fail with obscure compiler errors. The package automatically runs `xcodebuild -license accept` during preparation.

### Initial Selfupdate Requirement
*Reference: provision.star:36-47*

MacPorts requires `sudo port selfupdate` immediately after installation to sync the local ports database. Without this critical step, all port installations will fail because the ports tree is empty.

### PATH Configuration
*Reference: provision.star:17-34*

Users frequently can't find the `port` command because `/opt/local/bin` isn't in their PATH. The package automatically adds MacPorts paths to common shell profiles.

### Architecture Settings After OS Upgrade
*Reference: MacPorts documentation*

After macOS upgrades, comment out `build_arch` and `universal_archs` settings in `/opt/local/etc/macports/macports.conf`. These settings can cause build failures when they reference the previous OS version.

### C++ Headers Issue (CLT 16.0+)
*Reference: MacPorts Problem Hotlist*

Command Line Tools 16.0+ can leave legacy C++ headers that cause build failures. Remove with: `sudo rm -rf /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/include/c++`

### Migration vs. Full Reinstall
*Reference: install.star rollback and MacPorts Migration guide*

For major OS upgrades, MacPorts 2.10.0+ supports automatic migration. For older versions or failed migrations, a full reinstall may be necessary: export port list, uninstall all ports, remove MacPorts, install new version, restore ports.

| Problem Hotlist | https://trac.macports.org/wiki/ProblemHotlist | Common issues and solutions |
| MacPorts Guide | https://guide.macports.org | Architecture and security model |
